title: How Training Budgets Reshape Inference Scaling, and Non-Gaussian Sources Flow to Data
subtitle: Budget internalization · Flow matching · Federated Muon · Deep linear dynamics
intro: The main reads examine how fixed rollout caps reshape test-time scaling and how Euler discretization behaves in flow matching with non-Gaussian sources. Briefs cover spectral optimization, revised architecture and data-scaling studies, and post-training systems. The classic uses deep linear networks to resolve learning plateaus.
window: November 17–20, 2026 (Philadelphia time, including new announcements and delayed indexing)

articles.paper: Budget Internalization: Fixed-Budget RLVR Trades Test-Time Scaling for In-Budget Accuracy
articles.authors: Ilia Zavidnyi · Alexander Kovrigin · Arina Puchkova · Kirill Gelvan · Sergey Titov
articles.title: A training cap becomes a stopping habit
articles.dateNote: v1 submitted November 19, 2026 ET · November 20 announcement
articles.evidence: Read training setup, budget curves, ablations and limitations

blocks.text: A fixed rollout cap B also changes behavior: across Qwen3.5-4B, Gemma4-E2B and Nemotron-3-Nano-4B, GRPO improves accuracy near the cap while contracting the benefits of longer reasoning. [1]

blocks.tex: r_B(y)=\mathbf1\{y\text{ is correct}\}\mathbf1\{y\text{ finishes within }B\},\qquad A_B(b)=\mathbb E[\mathbf1\{\text{correct at evaluation cap }b\}]
blocks.label: Simplified notation for censored rewards; A_B(b) is accuracy at evaluation cap b after training with cap B, not the full GRPO objective.
The sign reversal below is an empirical finding, not a universal theorem.

blocks.text: The table uses Table 3 ablations: Qwen3.5-4B, DeepScaleR, an 8K training cap, at most 300 steps and 32 prompts × 8 rollouts per step. AIME 2024/25 contains 60 problems; avg@16 is mean correctness over 16 generations per problem (%), not pass@16. [1]

SFT on artificially truncated traces also reproduces internalization; naturally completed short traces do not show the same contraction. Strong KL and forced answers retain more high-budget capability while sacrificing in-budget gains. [1]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: The ± values are problem-level 95% intervals. These ablations each use one training seed; the main DeepScaleR comparison separately uses three. Evidence implicates length censoring but does not establish an explicit internal representation of B. [1]

articles.paper: Flow Matching from Non-Gaussian Sources: A Theory of Efficient Sampling
articles.authors: Yuchen Zhou · Lili Zheng · Yuxin Chen · Gen Li
articles.title: Non-Gaussian sources: which sampling error is controlled?
articles.dateNote: v1 submitted November 19, 2026 ET · November 20 announcement
articles.evidence: Read the model, Assumptions 1–3, Theorem 1 and proof outline; affiliation confirms Wharton’s Yuxin Chen

blocks.text: Flow matching and rectified flow (2023) learn transport velocities by regression. Heavy-tailed or mixture sources are allowed; the question is how finitely many velocity evaluations control Euler error. [2]

blocks.tex: Z\sim P_0,\quad X_\star\sim P_1,\quad Z\perp X_\star,\qquad X_t=(1-t)Z+tX_\star,\qquad v_t(x)=\mathbb E[X_\star-Z\mid X_t=x]
blocks.label: Independent linear interpolation and its population velocity field.
Sampling starts at a positive t₀ and stops early at tₙ<1; the grid refines near both endpoints.

blocks.text: Assume a positive C¹ source density, an L-Lipschitz score and finite V₀; the target second moment is bounded by a fixed power of (N+1) times V₀, with Assumption 3’s endpoint and step-size conditions. Theorem 1 gives: [2]

blocks.tex: \operatorname{TV}(\mathcal L(Y_N),\mathcal L(X_{t_N}))\leq\frac{CL(d+\log N)V_0\log^2 N}{N},\qquad N=\widetilde O(LdV_0/\varepsilon)
blocks.label: The guarantee targets the early-stopped interpolant. The proof accumulates one-step errors using TV contraction and restricted injectivity of non-Gaussian Euler maps.

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: The analysis uses the exact population velocity and does not cover estimation error. The target may be singular, so the bound cannot be rewritten as TV≤ε against the original P₁. [2]

articles.title: GUI grounding: coverage versus selection
articles.dateNote: v1 submitted November 18, 2026 ET · November 20 announcement

blocks.text: Controlled changes to cropping, instruction information and candidate sampling separate bottlenecks. articles.title: CaRR reuses the existing edit trajectory

blocks.text: CaRR refills replaced tokens and recovers submittable answers from the existing trajectory. At one-eighth of the full forward budget, mean accuracy over six metrics rises 7.44 percentage points. Abstract only; no extra backbone forwards does not imply zero system overhead. [6]

articles.paper: Optimizer-dependent training dynamics converge to the same one-third optimal data scaling
articles.authors: Hyunseok Lee · Mihir Basil · Yizhou Liu · Jeff Gore
articles.title: The one-third exponent: newly explicit boundaries
articles.dateNote: First posted September 29, 2026 · v2 November 19, 2026 ET

blocks.text: v2 adds a discrete Lyapunov stability condition, learning-rate fits for seven optimizers and a discussion of Adam features absent from the theory. In the fixed-teacher, single-softmax model, radial/tangential dynamic exponents remain distinct from optimal data scaling; this is not universal D⁻¹ᐟ³ for arbitrary LLMs. [11] [21]

articles.paper: Learning from Transients: Linear RNN Scaling Laws in Stationary Prediction
articles.authors: Ziyan Chen · Linhe Zheng · Peilin Liu · Zhongzhu Zhou · Ding-Xuan Zhou
articles.title: Linear RNNs: transients under a fixed stationary target
articles.dateNote: First posted August 23, 2026 · v3 November 18, 2026 ET
articles.evidence: Compared model and proof revisions in v2/v3

blocks.text: v3 reformulates the fixed stationary prediction setting and expands spectral comparisons and noncommuting filter-perturbation proofs. Heavy-tailed initialization can alter finite-time bias; constant-length trajectories attain the optimal risk order in the theorem-controlled range. Assumptions include stable linear-Gaussian dynamics and aligned power-law spectra. [12] [22]

classic.title: Deep linear networks: where do plateaus come from?
classic.paper: Exact solutions to the nonlinear dynamics of learning in deep linear neural networks
classic.authors: Andrew M. Saxe · James L. McClelland · Surya Ganguli
classic.dateNote: Historical classic · First posted December 20, 2013; read v3, February 19, 2014; ICLR 2014
classic.evidence: Read Sections 1.1–2, Equations 2–15 and Figure 3; exact solutions and their assumptions

recognition.label: 1,849 citations in the queried OpenAlex record (checked November 20, 2026)

classic.question: If inputs are not whitened and the singular basis of Σᵧₓ is not aligned with Σₓₓ, which cross-mode coupling breaks the plateau first?

blocks.text: Depth makes parameter dynamics nonlinear even when the input-output map stays linear. Following Baldi–Hornik’s (1989) loss geometry, Saxe et al. (2014) solve a family of trajectories to explain plateaus and rapid transitions. [18]

blocks.label: Whitened inputs, squared loss and singular modes representable by the hidden layer. Below, τ is the time scale of continuous gradient flow.
The paper’s dynamics: the linear end-to-end map produces coupled cubic weight equations.

blocks.text: Use the special aligned initialization W₁=R diag(a)Vᵀ and W₂=U diag(b)Rᵀ, with orthogonal hidden modes and RᵀR=I. This defines an invariant manifold with independent modes: [18]

blocks.label: The paper’s decoupled equations; subtracting the derivatives gives conserved interlayer imbalance.
Exact solution for a balanced, aligned mode. Small u₀ yields a plateau followed by a sharp rise; modes with larger singular value s learn earlier.
The paper’s depth notation rewritten as L weight matrices. Depth changes escape dynamics near small u while preserving the class of linear end-to-end maps.

blocks.text: Figure 3 compares the exact curves with randomly initialized linear and tanh networks on 32 orthogonal inputs; agreement for the latter two is approximate. The queried OpenAlex record shows 1,849 citations on November 20, 2026; other same-title records were not merged. [18] [19]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Exact solutions require whitening, alignment and continuous time. Numerical agreement for random initialization and nonlinear networks is not a theorem beyond these assumptions. Finite-step stability also constrains the interpretation of the depth limit. [18]
